source_policy: SEER Cancer Stat Facts, ACS Cancer Facts & Figures 2026, USPSTF. Citable; refresh yearly. NCCN not used.

incidence.us_annual_new_cases: ~321,910 new invasive cases in women (plus ~60,730 DCIS) projected for 2026; ~2,670 in men (ACS)
incidence.rank_among_cancers: 2nd most common cancer diagnosis overall; most common cancer in women
incidence.trend: Incidence rising ~1% per year over the past decade; steeper (~1.4%/yr) in women under 50

mortality.trend: Death rates down ~44% from 1989 through 2022, attributed to earlier detection and improved treatment

risk_factors.detail: Median age at diagnosis ~63; risk rises with age

risk_factors.factor: germline BRCA1/2 and other pathogenic variants
risk_factors.detail: Substantially elevated lifetime risk; informs risk-reducing strategies
First-degree family history; high-dose chest radiation before age 30
High mammographic density; atypical hyperplasia; prior DCIS/LCIS
Early menarche/late menopause, nulliparity or first child after 30, combined menopausal hormone therapy
Excess body weight (esp. postmenopausal), alcohol, physical inactivity

screening.guideline_summary: USPSTF (2024) recommends biennial screening mammography for average-risk women 40-74. ACS offers annual options beginning at 45 with earlier choice from 40. High-risk women may begin earlier with MRI. Cite USPSTF/ACS; NCCN not used.
screening.notes: Start age and interval remain areas of active debate; supplemental screening for dense breasts is evolving

epidemiology.presentation: Often detected on screening before symptoms; symptomatic presentation includes a palpable mass, skin or nipple change, or nipple discharge
